question: After the 11:05Z rollout the public API returns 502/503 for every request. What broke?

plan.rationale: Every request is answered with 502/503 right after the 11:05Z rollout on the public API: read the ECS service log group for the ALB target error and the task-definition change. The catalog lists no authorized database for this service, so logs are the only useful source.

hypotheses.statement: The 11:05Z rollout registered task definition revision public-api:43 with containerPort 8081, but target group api-tg still forwards to port 8080, so the public API answers 502/503 for every request because the balancer's connection to the targets is refused.
arguments_for: The ALB log records target 10.0.4.23:8080 connection refused with healthy 0/3 in target group api-tg
The ECS log records task-definition public-api:43 containerPort 8081 (previous revision 42: 8080) applied at the start of the rollout
The service reports its tasks RUNNING, so the targets exist and listen on the new port rather than failing to start

hypotheses.statement: The new tasks crash during startup after the rollout, so the target group has no live backend left to serve requests.
arguments_for: Every request returns 502/503 immediately after the rollout
arguments_against: The tasks are RUNNING and the ALB log shows a refused TCP connection to 10.0.4.23:8080, which means a live target was reached on a port it no longer listens on
The ECS log states the containerPort change explicitly (8081, previously 8080), so the failure is a port mismatch rather than a missing backend

findings.title: ALB target group forwards to port 8080 while revision 43 listens on 8081
findings.detail: Task definition revision public-api:43 moved the container port from 8080 to 8081 during the 11:05Z rollout, but target group api-tg still forwards to port 8080. The balancer gets connection refused from the new tasks (healthy 0/3) and answers 502/503 for every request. The tasks are RUNNING and the port change is explicit in the ECS log, so the requests reach a live task on the wrong port — this is a listener/target-port mismatch, not an application crash and not a missing backend.
findings.recommendation: Roll the api service back to revision 42 (containerPort 8080) or update target group api-tg to forward to port 8081, then confirm 3/3 targets report healthy and the 502/503 rate returns to baseline.

citations.excerpt: The ALB is a messenger: a 502 means the target answered badly or died mid-response, a 503 means no healthy target could take the request, a 504 means the target never answered in time.

demo_script.summary: Root cause confirmed: revision 43 of the api task definition moved the container port to 8081 while target group api-tg still forwards to 8080, so the balancer's connections are refused and clients see 502/503 for every request. The application-crash hypothesis is refuted because the tasks are RUNNING and the port change is explicit in the ECS log.
